articles.title: Man City: Prime Minister Andy Burnham to release details of his meetings with Man City owners
articles.summary: Andy Burnham has faced criticism for comments he made in the wake of Manchester City being found guilty of all charges related to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules.
articles.body:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he will release details of his meetings with senior figures at Manchester City following criticism of his comments in the wake of the club being found guilty of all charges related to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules.

An independent commission found City had broken rules over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018 by creating "sham" contracts with commercial partners to secretly funnel more than £830m into their football operations.

Burnham's previous role as mayor of Greater Manchester has led to questions about his relationship with City's Abu Dhabi ownership, with Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch demanding No 10 release all details of meetings between the prime minister and senior figures at the club.

"I've been asked by the leader of the opposition to publish details of my meetings, which I'm happy to do and I'm going to," Burnham told the Rest is Politics podcast.

"I will quite clearly put out there everything that I have done working with them in my previous role as Mayor of Greater Manchester.

"None of it is recent, actually, in terms of the meetings I had. I only had one significant meeting, actually, and that was in 2021."

The prime minister initially told the BBC he would be "really concerned" if Manchester City's owners decide to sell up following the guilty verdict before later denying his reaction had "downplayed the seriousness of the findings".

However, some Premier League clubs were so "astonished" by Burnham's stance that sources told BBC Sport they were "concerned" about political interference in the appeal process.

Sanctions are yet to be announced and City have lodged an appeal against the verdict.

City returned to action for the first time since the guilty verdict when they played at Liverpool on Sunday, winning 3-0 .

Clubs fear political interference in Man City appeal

Premier League: Man City face Liverpool at raucous Anfield in first game since guilty verdict

Burnham was mayor of Manchester from 2017 until earlier this year and his tenure took place during a sustained period of success for City.

As mayor, he championed investment from the Gulf as a way of growing Manchester's economy, a strategy which was initially pursued by the city's leaders before Burnham became the inaugural elected mayor of the Greater Manchester Combined Authority.

"I don't think I misspoke," said Burnham of his past comments on Man City's owners.

"What I would say is my mind hadn't been on all of the issues. My mind had been on Labour Party conference and I was doing interviews in relation to it.

"And also, I didn't link those two things. You know, the questions linked those two things. What I would say is they're very separate.

"The football issues are different from the investment issues. People will try and conflate those two things, but they shouldn't, in my view.

"The football issues, the findings of the independent commission are serious, as I said in the interview."

The entire process involving the charges against Manchester City is independent of the Premier League.

An independent commission held a 42-day hearing in 2024 which led to the verdict announced last month, with City also guilty of all charges except one relating to non-cooperation with the Premier League investigation.

The commission's report said that "a number of important club witnesses gave false evidence in key respects and that some knowingly gave untrue and dishonest evidence".

A separate independent appeal board will hear City's appeal. The club continues to deny any wrongdoing.

articles.title: AP College Football Poll 2026 Week 7 Rankings Released with Top Risers and Fallers
articles.summary: Georgia is the new overwhelming choice for the top spot in the Associated Press Top 25 poll following a chaotic Saturday of action.
articles.body:
Georgia is the new overwhelming choice for the top spot in the Associated Press Top 25 poll following a chaotic Saturday of action.

The Bulldogs held on to beat SEC rival Alabama 20-17 on the road, and Texas' 27-24 loss to Oklahoma cleared the way for Kirby Smart's squad.

The AP voters responded by dropping the Longhorns from first to seventh. The Tide didn't go anywhere and remain in sixth.

And the Longhorns' fall wasn't the only notable change to the Week 7 poll.

For LSU and Oregon, Week 6 didn't eliminate them from the College Football Playoff race, but they have almost no margin for error from this point forward. They're 22nd and unranked respectively.

The Tigers allowed 401 yards to Kentucky, and Will Stein's overtime gamble propelled the Wildcats to a dramatic 35-34 win. After a CJ Baxter touchdown run, the coach didn't settle for the point-after attempt and went for the victory. Quarterback Kenny Minchey had a wide-open lane to the end zone to give Lane Kiffin his second defeat since going to Baton Rouge.

LSU has Mississippi State, Alabama, Texas and Tennessee ahead on the schedule. Running the table would definitely earn the team a top-12 place by season's end, but there are a lot of spots for the Tigers to suffer another costly stumble.

Oregon has an easier slate the rest of the way, yet little from the Ducks' first five games inspires a lot of confidence.

Starting for an injured Dante Moore, Dylan Raiola didn't even make it through the entire game. He got benched for Brock Thomas after going 6-of-19 for 43 yards and two interceptions.

An Oregon defense that returned a ton of talent allowed UCLA to possess the ball for more than 39 minutes. Bruins running back Wayne Knight went for 103 yards on 22 carries.

This was supposed to be the year everything came together for coach Dan Lanning. The Ducks reached the CFP semifinals a season ago and then invested heavily in the roster, raising hopes of a championship run.

Instead, Lanning is left preaching patience to the fanbase and major donors:

Patience is at least something Jon Sumrall will have in abundance in Gainesville. The honeymoon period is over for the Florida coach, though.

The Gators fell to 4-2 with a 38-19 home loss to South Carolina as their defense was once again their undoing.

Two weeks ago, Florida moved up to eighth in the AP poll, its highest position since 2020. Maybe Sumrall proves to be the guy to make the program a title contender again. He clearly needs more than one season to make that happen.

articles.title: Asiste Modric y marca Rabiot... pero el Milan 'pincha'
articles.standfirst: Los 'rossoneri' son quintos a cuatro puntos de Inter y Lazio
articles.summary: Los 'rossoneri' son quintos a cuatro puntos de Inter y Lazio
articles.body: El Milan continúa invicto en Serie A, pero los de Rúben Amorim volvieron a dejarse dos puntos en su visita al Sassuolo (2-2). Un empate que deja a los 'rossoneri' quintos, a cuatro puntos de Inter y Lazio. Sorprendió Amorim dejando en el banquillo de inicio a Luka Modric. Se le echó en falta. Lo único destacado del arranque fueron las lesiones de Matteo Gabbia (20') y Fedde Leysen (27'). En el 32', un cabezazo alto de Adrien Rabiot a la salida de una falta lateral botada por Christian Pulisic, rompió la monotonía. Las mayores jugadas de peligro se concentraron cerca del añadido. Gonçalo Ramos rozó el gol por partida doble en el 43': primero se sacó un obús con la zurda que despejó Muric con problemas y acto seguido conectó un cabezazo a centro de Chukwueze que obligó a lucirse a Muric. El Sassuolo, encerrado, logró sobrevivir hasta el descanso gracias a Muric. El meta despejó un tiro a la media vuelta de Diego Moreira (49') y luego se lanzó abajo para desviar un cabezazo abajo de Pavlovic (51'). Tan mal lo debió ver Amorim que decidió sacar a Modric nada más comenzar el segundo tiempo. Tuvo el 1-0, sin embargo, Adzic en el 59'. Lo evitó, lanzándose con todo, Maignan. Llegado el minuto 63 apareció Modric. Recibió de Pulisic y filtró un pase al espacio para que Rabiot, de zurda, fusiltara a Muric. Tres goles y dos asistencias suma el internacional francés. Modric, por su parte, se anota su primer pase de gol. El Milan, con 0-1, se echó atrás. Maignan se reivindicó con dos nuevas paradas en el 66', la primera a tiro de Berardi y, a continuación, para frenar el taconazo de Thorstvedt. Nada pudo hacer, en cambio, en el 68'. Sacó de esquina Lauriente, no despejó nadie y marcó en el área pequeña Cas Odenthal. Movió ficha Amorim... pero el marcador ya no se movería. Sólo el joven Alphadjo Cissé inquietó a Muric en el 82' con un buen disparo. El Milan no termina de coger velocidad de crucero.

articles.title: AP Top 25: Georgia moves to No. 1 after Texas loss, Florida and Oregon drop out of poll
articles.summary: The Bulldogs got all but three first-place votes.
articles.body:
Georgia is the clear new No. 1 team in the AP Top 25.

The Bulldogs got all but three of the 69 first-place votes in Sunday's post-Week 6 poll after beating Alabama 20-17 in Tuscaloosa on Saturday night. The Tide stayed at No. 6 after the loss.

Texas, which lost 27-24 to Oklahoma on a field goal as time expired, dropped six spots to No. 7.

Behind Georgia, Notre Dame, Miami, Ohio State and Indiana fill out the top five. The Irish, Buckeyes and Hoosiers all won in Week 6. Miami was off.

After Texas, BYU stayed at No. 8 ahead of Ole Miss and Texas Tech at No. 10. The Red Raiders are in the top 10 after LSU's loss to Kentucky. The Tigers dropped 12 spots to No. 22 following the loss.

Kentucky is back in the top 25 this week after that win. The Wildcats were No. 24 after Week 4, but somehow dropped out of the poll following an overtime win at South Carolina. Now, UK is No. 15 and one of nine SEC teams in the top 16.

Both Oregon (No. 13) and Florida (No. 16) fell out of the top 25 entirely after home losses. The Ducks lost 17-15 to UCLA after committing seven turnovers without starting QB Dante Moore available because of his Week 4 concussion. Florida lost to a South Carolina team that was 0-3 in SEC play.

The Bruins jumped up nine spots to No. 12 after the win. UCLA should have moved up. But a nine-spot jump is especially curious given voters' opinion of Oregon. If the Ducks aren't a top-25 team, how is a two-point win over a team that's now unranked worth that big of a jump?

Next Saturday is set to be the biggest weekend of the season. So far.

There are two top-10 matchups with No. 4 Ohio State at No. 5 Indiana and No. 2 Notre Dame at No. 8 BYU. Additionally, Alabama visits No. 14 Tennessee, No. 9 Ole Miss hosts No. 13 Missouri, No. 16 Mississippi State goes to LSU, and No. 18 Oklahoma State heads to No. 20 Houston.

Clear your calendar. The day could be epic.

articles.title: El Mallorca vence y convence
articles.standfirst: Recupera sensaciones y se reencuentra con la victoria en el mejor partido de la temporada ante una mermada UD, cuyo técnico De la Barrera queda en la cuerda floja
articles.summary: Supera en Son Moix a una mermada Las Palmas, cuyo técnico Rubén de la Barrera se queda en la cuerda floja
articles.body: El Mallorca se reencuentra con la victoria tras dos jornadas sin ganar y sin marcar al derrotar en Son Moix a Las Palmas, cuyo técnico Rubén de la Barrera se queda en la cuerda floja tras los goles de Pablo Torre, Álex Sala y Adri Fuentes. Y es que los amarillos, con muchas bajas, eso sí, enlazan cuatro jornadas sin ganar y un solo triunfo en las últimas siete, pese al golazo de Iván Jaime. Empezaba el partido para el Mallorca como quien es consciente de que tiene que dar la vuelta a una situación por lo menos en cuanto a lo sensacional se refiere. Muy incisivo en la presión tras pérdida, en zonas de mucho peligro. Alex Sala fue el primero en probar la solvencia de Caro bajo palos con un disparo desde la frontal del área que blocó sin problemas el portero del conjunto canario. La UD quiso reaccionar con una transición rápida que no acabó en disparo, pero sí supuso una ocasión de peligro en las botas de Miyashiro. Precisamente el ex del Córdoba protagonizó el segundo acercamiento bermellón con otro disparo desde la frontal del área en el minuto 20 de juego, pero esta vez se marchaba desviado. Al tercer intento y, tras otro robo en el último tercio de Josep Cerdá, el de Pollença encontró a Pablo Torre dentro del área para que el cántabro anotara el primero del partido con un disparo ajustado al larguero. Un gol que redondeaba la que probablemente haya sido la mejor primera parte de los de Luis García. El Mallorca tuvo tiempo todavía de anotar otro gol que anuló el VAR por fuera de juego milimétrico de Liso antes de darle el balón a Álex Sala en una primera parte en que la que el conjunto de Rubén de la Barrera se ha visto superado sobre todo debido al poco balón que han podido tener por el dominio local. La segunda parte comenzaba con una imagen curiosa, ya que el conjunto canario tardaba más de la cuenta en regresar al terreno de juego tras el descanso, provocando el enfado de la afición bermellona. Una vez reanudado el choque, el Mallorca mantenía la iniciativa. Los locales avisaban primero en una acción a balón parado, con un envío de Álex Sala hacia Adri Fuentes cuyo cabezazo lo detenía Caro. No tardó en llegar el premio, cuando Álex Sala ampliaba la ventaja tras una buena dejada de Adri Fuentes con un derechazo desde la frontal ajustado al poste, culminando una acción que reflejaba la superioridad local. Con el 2-0, el Mallorca parecía tener el encuentro bajo control. Luis García movía el banquillo dando entrada a Alberto Moreno y Zito Luvumbo por Toni Lato y Josep Cerdà. Los bermellones incluso rozaban la sentencia en una acción de Adri Fuentes, que acababa chocando contra el poste cuando intentaba marcar el tercero. Sin embargo, cuando todo parecía encaminado, llegaba el golpe de Las Palmas. Una pérdida evitable de Luvumbo en un contragolpe muy favorable para el Mallorca terminaba castigando a los locales, ya que Iván Jaime aprovechaba la acción para conectar un disparo potentísimo que golpeaba el larguero antes de entrar. Un auténtico golazo que devolvía la incertidumbre al encuentro. El tanto visitante complicaba momentáneamente un partido que el Mallorca había dominado. Luis García introducía a Sergi Darder por Pablo Torre y, posteriormente, a Calatayud y Guille Fernández por Álex Sala y Antonio Sánchez. Finalmente acabó llegando la tranquilidad definitiva tras una recuperación en campo contrario, Darder encontraba a Adri Fuentes con un buen pase y el delantero definía con una preciosa vaselina ante la salida de Caro, estableciendo el definitivo 3-1. El Mallorca cerraba así una victoria merecida, mostrando una versión convincente y generando ocasiones suficientes para haber sentenciado antes. Tres puntos importantes para los bermellones, que sabían reaccionar cuando Las Palmas amenazaba con meterse de nuevo en el partido.

articles.title: I’m so proud – Haaland hails City win after rules breach judgement
articles.summary: Erling Haaland spoke of his pride after Manchester City claimed victory amid a hostile reception at Anfield. In their first match since the club were found g...
articles.body:
Erling Haaland spoke of his pride after Manchester City claimed victory amid a hostile reception at Anfield.

In their first match since the club were found guilty of multiple breaches of Premier League financial rules, City, who have appealed against the ruling, defeated 10-man Liverpool 3-0 on Sunday.

City's players were booed throughout but thrived in the atmosphere, with Haaland scoring the first of three quickfire goals after Ryan Gravenberch was sent off midway through the second half.

The reaction at the end was one of jubilation from everyone in City blue, with Haaland spending several minutes soaking in the celebrations of the visiting supporters.

He told Sky Sports: "For every single fan, this is a lovely moment which will stay with us for a long time when it comes to the feeling after the game and in the game.

"It was tough and it was hard, but we showed amazing character. I'm so proud of everyone."

Midfielder Elliot Anderson hailed City's courage, adding: "I think we've shown real togetherness and fight.

"It's a tough place to come and it's challenging and we really stuck together out there, fought for each other and played well as well. I think we've shown courage here."

Asked about the booing from Liverpool fans, Anderson added: "It was definitely more than normal, arriving in and the first 10 minutes of the game, but I thought we did really well to quieten the crowd."

Haaland, though, argued it was not that different to a regular game at Anfield, saying: "Not really, it's always tough to come here.

"With the Pep (Guardiola) and (Jürgen) Klopp era, it was so tough for both teams.

"It's about these times, stay strong mentally, stick together and do what you can do something about, and what we can do something about is to play good football and to fight together."

For former City defender-turned-pundit Micah Richards, the players came up with the perfect response to everything that has been piled on them since the news broke. Demotion is one possible penalty.

"All they could do was play football to the best of their ability," he said.

"When you're in a dressing room and there's accusations gone in, to the players – and it's not the club, it's the players who are getting a lot of the abuse – they wanted to go there and put on a show. That's exactly what they did today.

"We talked about how are they going to react to all the noise and that was just a perfect performance."

articles.title: Isco desactiva la rebelión rojilla
articles.standfirst: El malagueño, con un doblete, evita que Osasuna complete una remontada que tenía a punto
articles.summary: El malagueño, con un doblete, evita que Osasuna complete una remontada que tenía a punto
articles.body: El Betis ha sumado tres valiosísimos puntos a la vuelta del parón de selecciones en un partido completamente loco ante Osasuna, con dosis de polémica, y en el que los rojillos, después de ponerse 3-0 por debajo en el marcador, a punto estuvieron de completar la remontada. Isco salió al rescate de su equipo para evitar que la siesta le saliera carísima a los verdiblancos... y el joven Morante, en su debut, puso la rúbrica para el 5-2 final. Con su victoria, el equipo de Pellegrini alcanza los 19 puntos en la clasificación, conserva el tercer puesto, sólo por detrás de Barcelona y Atlético de Madrid, y logra mantener la velocidad de crucero en la que marchaba antes de las tres semanas de fecha FIFA. Los de Ramis, por su parte, no levantan cabeza. Acumulan cuatro derrotas y un empate en sus cinco últimos partidos. Aunque su segunda parte de hoy, poniendo en serios apuros a todo un Betis de Champions, debe ser su ejemplo a seguir para reconducir su camino en LaLiga. Con un llenazo hasta la bandera en las gradas y doble homenaje en la previa, a Marc Roca por su partido 100 con el Betis y a Álvaro Valles como mejor portero de LaLiga del pasado mes, los verdiblancos arrancaron el partido un tanto sorprendidos por el plan de juego de Osasuna. El conjunto rojillo esperaba en tres cuartos de su propio campo, intentaba cerrar espacios entre líneas y renunciaba por completo al balón, convirtiendo el duelo en un monólogo de los de Pellegrini. El conjunto andaluz se lo tomó con calma, con pases de seguridad y evitando pérdidas que pudieran dar lugar a transiciones del equipo de Ramis. Y en su primer acercamiento con cierto peligro, encontraron el premio. No se había cumplido el minuto 10 cuando el Cucho prolongó de espuela un saque de banda de Bellerín para que Riquelme tirara un autopase y se fuera al césped después de recibir un clarísimo manotazo en la cara de Santos. Penalti sin necesidad de VAR. Isco, tirando de sangre fría y engañando a Aitor Fernández, abrió el marcador. Fue su quinto gol a Osasuna, convertido ya en una de sus víctimas favoritas. Y aunque los rojillos trataron de despertar tras el gol con un disparo de Raúl García que no encontró portería y con un testarazo de Budimir a centro de Moi Gómez que fue a las manos de Valles, el partido era claramente de dominio local y daba la sensación de que el segundo gol era cuestión de tiempo. No hubo que esperar demasiado. Riquelme apretó a Santos en la salida de balón de los navarros, el Betis recuperó en campo contrario, Cucho Hernández recibió entre líneas y tuvo tiempo para controlar y buscar la mejor opción. Y la encontró en el lado contrario del campo. Abde, completamente solo, recibió la pelota en carrera, se plantó en el área y batió a Aitor Fernández con un buen remate al palo más corto. Ese tipo de finalizaciones que hace un par de años tanto le costaban al marroquí. Si para Isco los rojillos se convertían en uno de los equipos a los que más goles le ha marcado en LaLiga, cinco, para Abde tres cuartos de lo mismo. Tres dianas ante sus ex, una en cada uno de sus tres últimos enfrentamientos. El resultado al descanso pudo haber sido incluso mayor. Diego Llorente no precisó en un remate de cabeza a centro de Fran García y de nuevo Isco, omnipresente y muy recuperado a nivel físico, tuvo en sus botas en dos ocasiones el gol. En la primera, tras un centro raso desde la derecha de Riquelme, el primer intento del malagueño se estrelló en la defensa y el segundo lo sacó Aitor Fernández con una parada valor gol. Y si buena fue esa intervención, mejor aún fue la mano que sacó abajo para impedir que el capitán bético convirtiera una espectacular volea con la zurda a centro del Cucho tras una veloz contra. Osasuna quería, poquito a poco se acercaba al área, pero no podía. Y con espacios el Betis es letal... Santos, que había cometido el penalti del 1-0 y perdido el balón en la jugada del 2-0, se quedó en el vestuario tras el descanso. Osambela entró en su lugar. Pero los consejos que Ramis diera a su equipo en el intermedio parecieron irse al traste a las primeras de cambio y de la forma más rocambolesca. Jugada de pizarra en una falta lanzada por Isco que prolonga el Cucho de cabeza, despeja también de cabeza Budimir, la pelota rebota en Diego Llorente y tras rozar de nuevo en el croata, se cuela en la portería rojilla. El tercero. El partido parecía completamente sentenciado con toda la segunda parte por delante. O al menos eso pensó el Betis, que se desconectó de una manera inexplicable y se complicó la vida. Una frivolidad de Bellerín, que quiso salir jugando desde atrás en la frontal de su área rodeado de rivales, provocó una pérdida que terminó en las botas de Budimir para que recortara distancias. Se señaló inicialmente fuera de juego de Rubén García, pero el VAR lo corrigió y el tanto subió al marcador. Y acto seguido, en una segunda jugada tras un córner, los verdiblancos tiraron muy mal la línea, Budimir le ganó el sitio a Fran García y Catena encontró la manera de poner el balón por encima de Valles para que Raúl García de Haro, completamente solo, lo empujara a la red. El canterano bético pidió perdón a la que fue su afición al tiempo que la bronca de La Cartuja por la siesta de su equipo y los nervios por lo apurado del marcador hacían acto de presencia. Con 3-2 en el marcador, Ramis cambió el plan. Movió el banquillo y pidió a su equipo tener más la pelota. Pero antes de comprobar si su idea funcionaba, el partido volvió a romperse. Riquelme recibió la pelota y cayó en el área, la pelota quedó suelta, ni Cucho acertó a rematar ni la defensa a despejar, y el más listo de todos, Isco, encontró el espacio para controlar y ponerla en el ángulo. Doblete... y lío tremendo con el banquillo de Osasuna reclamando al colegiado. Las protestas llegaron porque en el arranque de la jugada del Betis, Rubén García se fue al suelo en una disputa con Natan. Los rojillos pedían falta y expulsión del central brasileño, que era el último defensor, los béticos insistían en que era una carga legal. El caso es que las explicaciones del aragonés Carlos Muñiz no convencieron nada a Ramis, pero el tanto subió al marcador para darle oxígeno a un Betis al que el partido se le había complicado muchísimo. Isco, antes de ser sustituido, estuvo cerca de firmar el 'hat-trick' en una contra. Mientras que Torró, con una volea en una acción de estrategia, volvió a poner el corazón en un puño a los más de 65.000 espectadores presentes hoy en La Cartuja. A partir de ahí, el partido bajó de revoluciones. Raúl se lesionó y se fue ovacionado. Morante debutó en LaLiga con el primer equipo... y el canterano dejó su sello con un golazo en el alargue. Lo celebró toreando de salón, en homenaje a su madre. Y los puntos se quedaron en Sevilla. Isco desactivó la rebelión rojilla antes de que se convirtiera en un incendio.

articles.title: There is one person to blame for the mess Man United are in, it’s not Michael Carrick
articles.summary: The tricky position Manchester United find themselves in, with six points from six games and their worst start to a league campaign in 40 years, will rightfu...
articles.body:
The tricky position Manchester United find themselves in, with six points from six games and their worst start to a league campaign in 40 years, will rightfully have supporters asking questions.

Chief among them: do INEOS really mean well for this team? If so, they must change a few things.

One area they need to rethink is their transfer strategy. Their determination not to overpay for targets, and to secure the best deals for players who genuinely want to join, deserves to be commended.

Their other approach, targeting Premier League talent for immediate impact, is paying off and proving a sound tactic.

As a result, Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha arrived and immediately raised the team's level. Youri Tielemans is harder to judge, having produced both strong and poor performances, so it is too early for a verdict.

Meanwhile, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba are yet to enjoy a sustained run of games that would show what they are really about. If everything clicks, these Premier League recruits should come in handy for the Red Devils, and that is what gives fans hope in that strategy.

Yet while United are building a stronger squad with a largely decent plan, one transfer idea is holding them back.

Bolstering one position each summer is proving a blunder in their squad planning. Instead of addressing real areas of concern, INEOS bolsters one position at a time, hoping to build a stronger team over time.

But how strong a side can you build when you are hell-bent on ignoring serious needs to stick to a predetermined plan? Last year, for example, former Man United head coach Ruben Amorim badly needed athletic midfielders, yet INEOS opted to strengthen the attack and made no effort to sign a midfielder.

They chose to pause that transfer need and revisit it a year later.

So you wait twelve months to address an obvious need, and other problems arise in the meantime.

Like other than bolstering the midfield, this summer, United also needed to reinforce the defence as well as the very attack they strengthened last year.

However, INEOS left those areas unaddressed because they were not part of the big summer plan.

Now the attack is suffering, with natural striker Benjamin Šeško out injured and likely to be sidelined for a lengthy spell, possibly requiring surgery. In defence, the team could have benefited from a top centre-back signing; the porous backline has been frustrating.

Still, at centre-back, one can argue it is about finding the right partnerships, given the many options there. However, the same cannot be said of left-back.

All of Luke Shaw 's back-ups are injured, and he himself was limping after the 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur. Clearly, the side needed another reliable left-back.

It is a tricky situation for the Red Devils, and one they will keep finding themselves in unless they are bold enough to address their real transfer needs rather than follow a plan that fails to solve them.

articles.title: El Prat será rival del Athletic en Copa y se jugará en L'Hospitalet
articles.standfirst: Se impuso 5-0 al CF Sant Rafel en la eliminatoria previa.
articles.summary: Se impuso 5-0 al CF Sant Rafel en la eliminatoria previa.
articles.body: El Prat se ha convertido en el rival del Athletic Club para la primera ronda de la Copa del Rey. El equipo catalán certificó su pase al torneo del KO tras endosar una contundente goleada por 5-0 al CF Sant Rafel en la eliminatoria previa. Sin embargo, el duelo copero frente a los leones vendrá acompañado de una mudanza obligada. El club ha emitido un comunicado informando a sus aficionados que no podrán disputar el partido en su feudo habitual, el Sagnier, debido a que las instalaciones no cumplen con el aforo mínimo requerido por la RFEF para albergar encuentros de esta competición. LA RFEF y el club han acordado que el partido contra el Athletic se juegue en el Estadio Municipal de L'Hospitalet. La directiva del Prat ha añadido que en los próximos días se ofrecerá toda la información detallada relativa al precio y la venta de las entradas para esta gran cita.

articles.title: Injury jinx costs 20-year-old Liverpool forward his big chance
articles.summary: Alexander Isak started the 2026/27 Premier League season with considerable swagger. The £125m signing from Newcastle was injured and out of form during his f...
articles.body:
Alexander Isak started the 2026/27 Premier League season with considerable swagger.

The £125m signing from Newcastle was injured and out of form during his first season at Anfield. Having experienced a proper preseason however he hit the ground running for Andoni Iraola.

The 27-year-old scored four top-flight goals before jetting out for international games with Sweden. Liverpool have suffered a setback however with the news that Isak would be sidelined with a minor injury picked up on international duty.

Iraola is already having to contend with the loss of Hugo Ekitike - with the Frenchman not expected to be back fit until around the turn of the year.

And any hopes the Reds will have had of turning to Cody Gakpo as an interim option at No9 have also been dashed.

The Dutchman was hurt during international duty for the Netherlands - leaving Iraola with a massive striking headache ahead of the Manchester City game on Sunday.

Lewis Koumas - a versatile young attacker - would be given the nod at No9. He is a relative novice in the position - particularly at Premier League level and given the scale of spending it's not ideal that the Merseysiders have such scant options up top right now.

And one player who may well be ruing an injury at a crucial time is Jayden Danns . Liverpool lost against Doncaster in the EFL Trophy during the week with 20-year-old forward Danns conspicuous by his absence.

Fielding questions after the game under-21 head coach Rob Page confirmed an injury concern for the promising frontman.

"He pulled up in training last week and felt something and wasn't quite comfortable," Page said according to the Liverpool Echo.

"So we're not going to take any chances, there's no need at all.

"He is all right, he has been training but we didn't think it was a risk we wanted to take. He's fit, and we thought it was better for him to have two training days rather than half-an-hour or 45 minutes in this game."

Another watershed moment for injury-hit Danns

There's every chance that Danns may have had an opportunity to showcase his credentials in the game against City on Sunday were it not for the latest injury strain.

He's already featured 10 times for Liverpool at senior level - scoring three goals - and hopes are high for what he might achieve in the game. But timing has never been kind to the forward - who has suffered from extensive injury trouble in his short career so far.

Instead of priming himself for a go against City he has been left kicking his heels and hoping to get back in once again at underage level.

This is another crossroads moment in the young career of Jayden Danns - who seemingly cannot compile a run of luck in terms of injuries at the moment.

articles.title: Man City must make 'own noise' amid financial scandal, says Maresca
articles.summary: Enzo Maresca said Manchester City must "make their own noise" to drown out the distraction of the guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking Premier Leag...
articles.body:
Enzo Maresca said Manchester City must "make their own noise" to drown out the distraction of the guilty verdict on over 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules.

In their first match since the bombshell ruling, City showed they are unfazed by the uncertainty over potential sanctions as they ignored the hostile Anfield atmosphere to beat 10-man Liverpool 3-0 on Sunday.

City boss Maresca has made a flawless start to the daunting task of replacing Pep Guardiola.

The Italian has won his eight games in all competitions to take City three points clear at the top of the Premier League.

But the future of City's title challenge likely rests on the outcome of the club's appeal against the verdict of an independent commission.

"It was not easy for the players after the last two or three weeks but they dealt with the situation very good," said Maresca.

"I said during the week we need to lean how to deal with the outside noise, but make our own noise, which is to win games.

"Our fans were singing at the end, so the noise was from us."

City took full advantage after a red card for Liverpool's Ryan Gravenberch on the hour mark swung the momentum their way.

Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki struck in a 13-minute spell after Gravenberch's dismissal as City won in front of a crowd at Anfield for only the second time since 2003.

"To win 3-0 at Anfield is a great result for sure. In this moment all the organisation needs this kind of win," added Maresca.

"It's good for us as a coaching staff, the players, the organisation. This kind of win is good for all the club."

Maresca also refuted suggestions that his celebrations would be tempered by the uncertainty of not knowing if the three points will ultimately matter at the end of the season.

"You cannot imagine how happy I am," he said.

"I am here to try to prepare the games and win the games. Hopefully, I can speak about this situation when we win the appeal."

The defeat was Andoni Iraola's first as Liverpool manager, but his side are now nine points off the top in ninth place.

The Reds were blunted by the absence of injured trio Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo.

Iraola, though, believed Liverpool were the better side until Gravenberch's controversial exit for two quickfire yellow cards.

"There were two different games. One until the red card and one from the red card until the end," said the Spaniard.

"We were the better team until the red card and they were better than us obviously after and scored the goals."

articles.title: Isco's Betis rise back above Real Madrid to third
articles.summary: Veteran playmaker Isco struck twice to help Real Betis climb back into third place in La Liga with a 5-2 win over Osasuna on Sunday.Earlier on Real Sociedad...
articles.body:
Veteran playmaker Isco struck twice to help Real Betis climb back into third place in La Liga with a 5-2 win over Osasuna on Sunday.

The Andalucian side moved a point above Real Madrid, fourth, and level with second place Atletico Madrid, trailing leaders Barca by five points.

Manuel Pellegrini's side claimed a sixth league win from eight matches with an exciting display of attacking football at La Cartuja stadium, where they are playing until their Benito Villamarin home is renovated, likely 2028.

Former Real Madrid midfielder Isco, 34, netted from the penalty spot after a foul on Rodrigo Riquelme, and Ez Abde doubled the hosts lead after half-an-hour with a cool finish.

Ante Budimir's own goal gave Betis their third after half-time, before the Croatian striker netted at the correct and Raul Garcia added another to give Osasuna a fighting chance.

Isco capitalised on a loose ball in the box to grab his second and Jose Morante bagged a fifth in stoppage time to close out Betis's big win.

Later Sunday Javier Aguirre takes charge of his first match at the helm of bottom-of-the-table Valencia as they visit Racing Santander.

Earlier on Real Sociedad defeated Deportivo La Coruna 3-2 in another entertaining battle.

The Basque side, sixth, eased into a three-goal lead Mario Soriano pulled one back for the visitors in San Sebastian to spark a Depor fight back.

They were given further encouragement when Real Sociedad's Pablo Marin was sent off in the 66th minute for a foul on Nsongo Bil in the box and Yeremay Hernandez netted from the penalty spot.

Both teams finished with 10 men after Lorenzo Amatucci brought down Mikel Oyarzabal as the last man, and Depor could not find an equaliser.

On Saturday Liga leaders Barcelona beat Getafe 3-0 to prolong their perfect start to the season, with eight wins from eight league games.

Hansi Flick's side are followed by second place Atletico Madrid, who snatched a late 2-1 win at Alaves, while Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid scraped a 1-0 victory over Villarreal despite Vinicius Junior's red card for hair-pulling.

articles.title: Man City blow Liverpool away at Anfield – but was it all meaningless?
articles.summary: Liverpool 0-3 Manchester City: Jeremy Doku transformed a strange game from the bench after Ryan Gravenberch was sent off for two yellow cards
articles.body:
Three brilliant finishes, and possibly the only ending this freak match was ever going to have.

Manchester City again abrasively drive on amidst it all, absolutely revelling in a 3-0 win at Liverpool , but nobody knows what it will actually mean.

Few, outside the City fans in the relished moments of celebration, even know what to feel.

It does highlight the very absurdity of the situation, as the Abu Dhabi-owned club get to have this act of defiance, and the rest of the league gets even more furious about it all.

City fans, for their part, also got to feel something "real" after the uncertainty over the past two weeks. Liverpool, like everyone else, are waiting for a clarity that now seems essential for this very season.

It was why the main impression from this game should not be regarding City's "brilliance". Really, after two weeks of build-up and debate about the Premier League "brand", we saw the real damage. This immediately felt untenable.

It only emphasises the need for this process to be concluded and - above all - why the sanctions should have been announced with the decision.

That would also add more of an incentive for both sides on the appeals process.

This is otherwise a farce for the Premier League, a bizarre unreality.

Except, this is far more serious than the light tone that City's inflatables lent.

None of that should be taken as one of those arguments that the Premier League should not have taken on this case like this.

The robustness of the league depends on it, a point further made by this strange, strange occasion.

Even if the football here was secondary to everything around it, the identity of the key players reflected so many of the arguments that are being made about how City have managed to construct squads like this; why the brilliance on display is so undercut by a case that is almost overwhelming.

Erling Haaland, one of the best-paid players in the world, whipped in a one-touch finish that fully showed his worth.

Jeremy Doku, supplying another of those exquisite finishes that have become part of an impressive repertoire, was a substitute who most other teams would love to have as a starter.

Rayan Cherki then danced through the wreckage in a manner that only added insult to injury.

Just before all of that, a Liverpool team already depleted by injury wilted once Ryan Gravenberch was sent off.

That was the key, coming at a crucial moment in the game.

It felt a very soft decision, for a second yellow card, if also a silly one from the midfielder.

Gravenberch had been playing well, offering the energy that Liverpool required.

Such sentences of course fit into the general football chat you would expect of a Super Sunday game and, in normal circumstances, you might talk about City gleaning profound confidence from such a commanding victory at Anfield.

Except, saying any of that seems ridiculous, since these were entirely abnormal circumstances.

Liverpool fans will still feel they had the last laugh, as they chanted "going down" at the final whistle.

Rather than immediately feeling like a volcano, Anfield instead rose to a high heat. The sense was of long-term frustration rather than fury.

This crowd has generally intended to support its own rather than sing about others, but this match was obviously when an exception was to be made.

Aside from the liberal sprinkling of "cheats" and "shams" across banners, there were more novel ones like "And after all, you've robbed us all", as well as one with pound signs to match the number of charges.

Among the chants were "going down" and "you know what you are".

City gleefully adopted the latter themselves, however, among a few other responses.

While a certain type of defiance and gallows humour is obviously entirely understandable from City fans, the feeling does change when the response is abrasively supportive of the ownership.

This is not some calamity that has been imposed upon them, after all.

It comes from the club's own acts, the words of its own people.

And they have, ultimately, been found guilty.

City are just opting to appeal that conclusion.

And, amid a lot of debate about what is "real" in all of this, the extent of City's defiance felt another mockery of the league. Or, as one football insider said, "that they get to do this, to have this stand".

More relevantly, it starts to complicate the argument around the fans also being victims, which they are.

The equation changes if you're this abrasive about it after the fact, especially when the strident argument for so long has been that the club would clear their name.

Hope in an appeal isn't the same as defiant belief in the ownership – especially given the potential implications of all.

There's also a strange incongruity between that and the very visible throwbacks to a more innocent time, through the inflatable bananas.

One message indicates a will to get back to simpler times.

The other is right in amongst all of this.

By the end, the away fans were singing "we love you City", as the Liverpool fans filtering out responded with "cheats".

The Kop had by then emptied, the sound system playing Fleetwood Mac's "Sweet Little Lies".

Just one more moment that made this day entirely unserious – and everything around it still so serious.

articles.title: Isco: "Hoy en día, en cinco minutos de desconcentración te hacen dos goles"
articles.standfirst: El capitán hace autocrítica después de que su equipo sufriera tras ponerse 3-0 ante Osasuna
articles.summary: El capitán hace autocrítica después de que su equipo sufriera tras ponerse 3-0 ante Osasuna
articles.body: Isco Alarcón fue elegido MVP en la victoria por 5-2 del Betis ante Osasuna. El marcador, holgado, no refleja la realidad de un partido que se le complicó muchísimo a los verdiblancos. Los de Pellegrini llegaron a ponerse 3-0 arriba, pero los rojillos recortaron distancias hasta el 3-2 acercándose a la remontada. Hasta que apareció el malagueño para apagar la rebelión y encarrilar un triunfo que analizó así en los micrófonos de Movistar LaLiga TV. Un partido loco: "Hemos tenido momentos muy buenos; creo que la primera parte y el inicio de la segunda con el tercer gol han sido buenos. Luego hemos tenido un momento que no se puede repetir, donde tenemos que controlar mejor el partido. Hoy en día, en cinco minutos de desconcentración te hacen dos goles, se te complica el partido y es algo que tenemos que corregir. Pero en líneas generales, estoy contento por los tres puntos, por la victoria y creo que ha sido un buen partido". Cómo se encuentra: "Contento, cada vez con más ritmo. Estas tres semanas me han dado tiempo para trabajar y ponerme a punto, que todavía me falta, pero trabajando con mucha ilusión, con muchas ganas de mejorar, de ayudar al equipo y se nos presenta una temporada muy ilusionante. La polémica previa a su segundo gol: "No la he visto. Al final, después de un montón de rebotes ahí en el área, he ido con fe, me ha caído el balón y he metido un gol importante porque se nos había puesto muy complicado. Ellos estaban apretando mucho y estoy contento sobre todo por la victoria". El debut de Morante: "Es un jugador que lo tiene todo: joven, con mucha proyección, mucha calidad, muy buen tiro y está en el equipo perfecto para crecer de la mejor manera posible. Tenemos que cuidarlo entre todos y seguro que nos va a ayudar mucho".

articles.standfirst: Andy Burnham, primer ministro británico, expuso que pronto sacarán a la luz los detalles de las reuniones mantenidas con la directiva 'cityzen'
articles.summary: Andy Burnham, primer ministro británico, expuso que pronto sacarán a la luz los detalles de las reuniones mantenidas con la directiva 'cityzen'
articles.body: El Manchester City, como dijo Maresca después de la goleada lograda en Anfield, tiene que tratar de frenar el ruido exterior que rodea al club en estos momentos. Desde las altas esferas del país, sin embargo, ya están empezando a pronunciarse. Uno de los que alzó la voz fue Andy Burnham, primer ministro británico, quien detalló que pronto sacarán a la luz los detalles de las reuniones mantenidas con la directiva 'cityzen'. Todo, después de las duras críticas que ha recibido por sus comentarios... una vez conocida la culpabilidad del Manchester City ante las acusaciones de la Premier. "El líder de la oposición me ha pedido que publique los detalles de mis reuniones, algo que haré con mucho gusto y que voy a hacer", declaró en el podcast de Rest is Politics. Cabe recalcar, eso sí, que Andy Burnham está en el centro de la polémica porque fue Alcalde de Mánchester antes de llegar al gobierno británico. "Voy a dejar bien claro todo lo que he hecho trabajando con ellos en mi anterior cargo como alcalde del Gran Manchester. En realidad, nada de esto es reciente, en lo que respecta a las reuniones que he tenido. Solo tuve una reunión importante, y fue en 2021".

articles.title: Dahl y Sudakov devuelven al Benfica a la senda de la 'Vitória'
articles.standfirst: Las 'águilas', segundas a cinco puntos del líder, se rehacen de su derrota ante el Oporto
articles.summary: Las 'águilas', segundas a cinco puntos del líder, se rehacen de su derrota ante el Oporto
articles.body: El Benfica se ha desquitado de su derrota contra el Oporto (3-1) justo antes del parón. La victoria sobre el Vitória Guimaraes (1-0) permite a las 'águilas' acostarse segundos, a cinco puntos de los 'dragones', que cuentan sus ocho partidos por triunfos. Fue un goleador nada habitual, Samuel Dahl, el que adelantó a los pupilos de Marco Silva en el 24'. El internacional sueco arrancó con potencia, tiró una pared con Vangelis Pavlidis y, mano a mano con Oliwier Zych, resolvió con clase: de vaselina. Pudo ampliar distancias el Benfica al poco de iniciarse la segunda mitad. Claudio Echeverri, que sustituyó a Andreas Schjelderup en el 63', se plantó mano a mano con Zych, pero el meta consiguió desviar a córner con el pie el tiro del ex del Girona. Fue, sin embargo, Georgiy Sudakov el que puso la firma al 2-0 en el 75'. Gianluca Prestianni atrajo a varios rivales en conducción antes de ceder para Echeverri, que, a su vez, descargó sobre el ucraniano. El ex del Shakhtar no tuvo piedad y fusiló desde la frontal para anotar su primer gol del curso.
